item_name: Impact on Others — Did any of the identified symptom(s) significantly disrupt care or living environment?

lookback_source.quote: Consider the previous review of the clinical record, staff interviews across all shifts and disciplines, interviews with others who had close interactions with the resident and previous observations of the behaviors identified in E0200 for the 7-day look-back period.

lookback_notes: The item's own Steps for Assessment page (p. E-11) states the behaviors identified in E0200 are considered for the 7-day look-back period. Counting convention comes from the general convention: "The ARD (item A2300) is the last day of the observation/look-back period, and day 1 for purposes of counting back" (p. 2-21), i.e., ARD plus the 6 previous calendar days.

coding_levels.label: No
coding_levels.definition: None of the identified behavioral symptom(s) significantly disrupted delivery of care or the living environment.

source.quote: Code 0, no: if none of the identified behavioral symptom(s) significantly disrupted delivery of care or the living environment.

coding_levels.label: Yes
coding_levels.definition: Any of the identified behavioral symptom(s) created a climate of excessive noise or interfered with the receipt of care or participation in organized activities by other residents.

source.quote: Code 1, yes: if any of the identified behavioral symptom(s) created a climate of excessive noise or interfered with the receipt of care or participation in organized activities by other residents.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code 0, no, if none of the identified behavioral symptom(s) significantly disrupted delivery of care or the living environment.

source.quote: Code 0, no: if none of the identified behavioral symptom(s) significantly disrupted delivery of care or the living environment.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code 1, yes, if any of the identified behavioral symptom(s) created a climate of excessive noise or interfered with the receipt of care or participation in organized activities by other residents.

source.quote: Code 1, yes: if any of the identified behavioral symptom(s) created a climate of excessive noise or interfered with the receipt of care or participation in organized activities by other residents.

federal_coding_rules.rule: For E0600C, code based on whether the behavior interferes with staff ability to deliver care or conduct organized activities, interrupts receipt of care or participation in organized activities by other residents, and/or causes other residents to experience distress or adverse consequences.

source.quote: For E0600C, code based on whether the behavior interferes with staff ability to deliver care or conduct organized activities, interrupts receipt of care or participation in organized activities by other residents, and/or causes other residents to experience distress or adverse consequences.

federal_coding_rules.rule: To code E0600, determine if the behaviors identified (in E0200) put others at significant risk of physical illness or injury, intruded on their privacy or activities, and/or interfered with their care or living environments.

source.quote: To code E0600, determine if the behaviors identified put others at significant risk of physical illness or injury, intruded on their privacy or activities, and/or interfered with their care or living environments.

federal_coding_rules.rule: E0600 (including E0600C) is completed only when E0300 is coded 1, yes (any of E0200A, E0200B, or E0200C coded 1, 2, or 3); when E0300 is coded 0, skip to E0800.

source.quote: Code 1, yes: if any of E0200A, E0200B, or E0200C were coded 1, 2, or 3. Proceed to complete Impact on Resident item (E0500), and Impact on Others item (E0600).

federal_coding_rules.rule: When E0200A, E0200B, and E0200C are all coded 0, E0300 is coded 0, no, and the assessor skips to E0800 (E0600 is not completed).

source.quote: Code 0, no: if E0200A, E0200B, and E0200C all are coded 0, not present. Skip to Rejection of Care—Presence & Frequency item (E0800).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Resident intent must not be taken into account when coding items in Section E; the section focuses on the resident's actions, not the intent of their behavior.

source.quote: Resident intent should not be taken into account when coding for items in this section.

federal.criterion: Review of the clinical record for the 7-day look-back period, considered together with prior staff interviews and observations of the behaviors identified in E0200.

source.quote: Consider the previous review of the clinical record, staff interviews across all shifts and disciplines, interviews with others who had close interactions with the resident and previous observations of the behaviors identified in E0200 for the 7-day look-back period.

federal.notes: Stated as step 1 of Steps for Assessment for E0600.

federal.criterion: Staff interviews across all shifts and disciplines, plus interviews with others who had close interactions with the resident.

federal.notes: Part of the required assessment steps for E0600.

federal.criterion: Documentation of subsequent assessments compared with a baseline to identify changes in the resident's behavior, including response to interventions.

source.quote: Subsequent assessments and documentation can be compared with a baseline to identify changes in the resident's behavior, including response to interventions.

federal.notes: Stated under Planning for Care rationale, not framed as a coding requirement.
